questions.text: What were the problems faced by Krishna Devaraya at the time of ascending the throne?

When he came to power, the kingdom faced various internal and external challenges.
Europeans arriving via new sea routes established their colonies.
Northern Mughals attempted to expand their empire southward.
The five Shahi kingdoms of the Bahmani dynasty became powerful sultans and engaged in wars with Krishnadevaraya.
Additionally, Ummattur and Orissa kings posed constant threats.

questions.text: Explain the military system of Vijayanagara Empire.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the military system of Vijayanagara Empire. (A)

answer.value:
Vijayanagara had a powerful army.
It consisted of three categories: permanent forces, troops sent by vassal states, and royal guards (for the king’s security).
Infantry, cavalry, elephants, and cannons were the main units.
Large elephants and Arabian horses were key attractions.
The army included a navy, and people of all religions could hold high ranks.

questions.text: Write a short note on the religious system of Vijayanagara Empire.
questions.text_as_printed: Write a short note on the religious system of Vijayanagara Empire. (A)

answer.value:
The Vijayanagara Empire is credited with promoting all religions equally.
Sri Vaishnavas and Jains lived in perfect harmony, forgetting their religious differences.
Early Vijayanagara kings supported Shaivism and Veerashaivism, while later kings encouraged Vaishnavism.
Mosques and dargahs were built for Muslims.
Vijayanagara kings developed trade with the Portuguese and permitted the construction of churches, promoting Christianity.

questions.text: Who was the most famous sultan of the Adil Shahis? What were his contributions?
questions.text_as_printed: Who was the most famous sultan of the Adil Shahis? What were his contributions? (D)

answer.value:
The most famous Adil Shahi king, Ibrahim II, ascended the throne at age 9.
His 47-year reign included historic events.
Politically, his efficient administration brought Bijapur to its zenith, with significant progress in art, literature, and education.
His book “Kitab-i-Navras” begins with praises of Lord Ganesha, Saraswati, Narasimha, and Prophet Muhammad.
The book reflects Ibrahim II’s scholarship, dignity, and religious tolerance.

questions.text: What were the achievements of Devaraya II?
questions.text_as_printed: What were the achievements of Devaraya II? (A)

answer.value:
The most famous Sangama dynasty king was Devaraya II.
He earned the title “Gaja Bentekara” (Hunter of Elephants).
He defeated Orissa’s king Gajapati Kapilendra and captured Kondaveedu.
By subduing regional leaders along the border, he extended the empire to the Krishna River in the northeast.
He defeated Kerala’s ruler and gained sovereignty over Kerala and Sri Lanka.

questions.text: Describe the art and architecture of the Vijayanagara period.
questions.text_as_printed: Describe the art and architecture of the Vijayanagara period. (A)

answer.value:
Vijayanagara kings continued the architectural style of the Chalukyas, Cholas, and Hoysalas.
Distinctive features include spacious assembly halls and marriage halls.
Temples had large gopurams (towers), ornate arches, and mandapas, emphasizing grandeur and elegance over decoration.
Rough granite was used for construction.
Temples were built in Hampi, Shringeri, Tirupati, Lepakshi, Karkala, Moodabidri, Bhatkal, Chidambaram, Kalahasti, Nandi, Srishaila, Kolar, and other places.
The Vidyashankara temple in Shringeri is unique in India.
The oldest Vijayanagara temple is the Virupaksha temple in Hampi.
The Vijaya Vitthala temple in Hampi is renowned for its architectural beauty, with musical pillars, grand marriage halls, and a stone chariot.
Krishnadevaraya built the Mahanavami Dibba in Hampi for the Dasara festival.
Kamal Mahal, Elephant Stable, and Queen’s Bath are excellent examples of Indo-Muslim architecture.
Statues of Lakshminarasimha, Kadalekallu Ganesha, Sasuvekallu Ganesha, and Uddana Veerabhadra are captivating.

questions.text: How can you say that ‘the economic system of the Vijayanagara Empire was prosperous’?
questions.text_as_printed: How can you say that ‘the economic system of the Vijayanagara Empire was prosperous’? (D)

answer.value:
Land revenue was the main source of income of the state.
Profession tax, house tax, road tolls, trade taxes, import-export duties, and tributes from feudatories were also sources of income.
There was great progress in the fields of industry and trade.
Spices like pepper, cloves, and cardamom, along with saltpetre, iron ore, diamonds, sugar, musk, sandalwood, and perfumes were exported.
Weaving was one of the major industries.
Gold coins like “Varaha,” “Gadyana,” and “Pagoda,” silver “Tara,” and copper coins like “Pana,” “Duddu,” and “Kasu” were in use.
Bhatkal, Honnavar, and Mangalore were important ports of the Vijayanagara Empire.
Foreign traders from Arabia, China, and Portugal had trade relations with the empire.

questions.text: Explain the military achievements of Krishna Devaraya.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the military achievements of Krishna Devaraya. (A)

answer.value:
As Robert Sewell noted, “Krishnadevaraya was an unparalleled warrior, skilled general, and political strategist. He won all wars and expanded his empire in the south.”
He defeated Gangaraja of Ummattur and captured the Shivanasamudra fort.
He captured the Raichur fort and helped the Portuguese army seize Goa from the Bijapur Sultan, establishing trade relations.
He attacked the Udayagiri fort, demonstrating his determination.
He captured Kalinga’s capital, Cuttack, and defeated Gajapati Prataparudra.
He signed a peace treaty with him.
Krishnadevaraya defeated Bijapur’s Adil Shahi and captured the Raichur fort.
While attacking Raichur, he encouraged soldiers, saying, “Everyone must die someday. If you die on the battlefield, you go to heaven. If you win, you are blessed.”
After capturing Raichur, he seized Bidar and Kalaburagi (Gulbarga) forts.
He defeated Bahmani’s Prime Minister Qasim Barid, released the Bahmani prince, imprisoned the Prime Minister in Bidar, and placed him on the Bahmani throne, earning the title “YavanarajyaPratishthapanacharya” (Establisher of the Yavana Kingdom).

questions.text: How was Muhammad Gawan an efficient Prime Minister of the Bahmani Kingdom?
questions.text_as_printed: How was Muhammad Gawan an efficient Prime Minister of the Bahmani Kingdom? (D)

answer.value:
During this period, Mohammad Gawan ruled the Bahmani kingdom with selflessness and dedication.
As Prime Minister, he elevated the Bahmani kingdom to great heights.
He studied Muslim religious texts and law in Cairo and was proficient in Arabic and Persian.
He served as Prime Minister under Bahmani kings Humayun, Nizam Shah, and Mohammad Shah III.
Through his efficient administration and coronation, he enhanced the Bahmani kingdom’s glory.
Gawan captured Konkan, Goa, and Belgaum, and later occupied Orissa and Kondaveedu.
In 1481, he invaded Kanchi and looted its vast wealth.
He fell victim to his enemies’ conspiracies and was executed on false charges of treason.

questions.text: Explain the contributions of Vijayanagara rulers to the field of literature.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the contributions of Vijayanagara rulers to the field of literature .(E)

answer.value:
Literature was produced in Kannada, Sanskrit, Telugu, and Tamil languages.
Ratnakaravarni’s “Bharatesha Vaibhava,” Chamarasa’s “Prabhulingaleele,” and Kumaravyasa’s “Karnata Bharata Kathamanjari” are major Kannada poems.
Bhimakavi wrote the Kannada version of Palkurike Somanatha’s Telugu work “Basava Purana.”
The collection of BasavadiShivasharanas’ vachanas, “Shunya Sampadane,” was compiled.
Lakkannadandesa’s “Shivatattva Chintamani,” Purandaradasa, Kanakadasa, Sripadaraya, and Vyasaraya enriched Dasara literature.
Kanakadasa’s “Mohanatarangini,” “Nala Charitre,” “Haribhaktasara,” and “RamadhanyaCharitre” are significant works.
In Sanskrit, Vidyaranaya’s “Shankara Vijaya” and “SarvadarshanaSangraha” were composed.
His brother Sayanacharya wrote “Vedartha Prakasha” (a commentary on the Vedas), “Ayurveda Sudhanidhi,” and “Purushartha Sudhanidhi.”
Gangadevi, wife of Kampanaraya, wrote “Madhuravijayam,” describing sacred places.
Allasani Peddana’s Manucharitramu, Timmana’s Parijataapaharanam, and Tenali Ramakrishna’s Ubhataradhya Charitramu – Telugu works

questions.text: List the contributions of the Bahmani and Shahi sultans to education and art.
questions.text_as_printed: List the contributions of the Bahmani and Shahi sultans to education and art. (A)

answer.value:
Contributions of the Bahmani and Shahi Sultans to Education and Art:
Promotion of education: Emphasis was given to Arabic and Persian education. Bidar and Bijapur became important centers of learning. Madrasas and mosques provided both religious and secular education.
Libraries: The madrasa established by Muhammad Gawan at Bidar had a rich collection of thousands of manuscripts.
Music and art: Ibrahim Adil Shah II composed the book Kitab-e-Navras and promoted Hindu-Muslim cultural harmony. They also patronized painting and miniature art.
Architecture: They built notable structures such as the Jama Masjid at Gulbarga, the Rangin Mahal at Bidar, and the world-famous Gol Gumbaz and Ibrahim Rauza.
Paranjyoti’s Tiruvilaiyadal Puranam – Tamil work
